items.title: TD Range Projection, TD Range Expansion Breakout, and TD Channels
ANATOMY OF THE RETEST IN THE QQQ OPENING RANGE BREAKOUT
items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper is an exploratory and descriptive study. The author makes no claims of causality or exploitability regarding the documented patterns. We present an exploratory study of the post-breakout sequence in the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF, using intraday data at one-minute resolution from January 2017 through December 2024. The existing literature on the Opening Range Breakout focuses on entry at the moment of the breakout; the internal dynamics of the minutes that follow have not been measured to date. We decompose the sequence into four levels-the opening range, the breakout, the retest, and the outcome-and document the statistical associations observed at each level. We find that range size is associated with the magnitude of the subsequent move, that a consistent fraction of breakouts generates a retest of the broken level within a defined time window, that the time elapsed until that retest shows the strongest association with the subsequent outcome, and that larger pre-retest excursions are associated with a lower probability of continuation-a counterintuitive pattern that we document along with its interpretive limitations. items.title: Regime-Conditional Alpha in SPY 0DTE Opening Range Breakout Strategies: A Filtering and Strike Selection Framework
items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents a simulation-based quantitative examination of the Opening Range Breakout (ORB) strategy applied to zero-days-to-expiration (0DTE) debit vertical spreads on the SPDR S&amp;P 500 ETF Trust (SPY). Using a transparent Monte Carlo simulation framework calibrated to empirically documented parameters across 756 potential trading days (2022-2025), we model 214 filtered trades and derive the conditions under which the strategy generates positive expected value. The simulation generates an unfiltered win rate of 46.8%, consistent with the practitioner literature, and a filtered win rate of 65.4% (95% Wilson CI: [58.8%, 71.5%]) under a three-factor filter stack: day-of-week selection (Monday, Wednesday, Friday), VIX regime restriction (15-25), and macroeconomic event exclusion. We derive an analytically exact breakeven win rate of 66.7% under fixed 25%/50% exit parameters and show that the observed filtered win rate sits at the margin of viability, emphasizing the fragility of the edge to execution slippage.
